대학교.ex: 제 동생은 서울에 있는 대학교에 다녀요.
대학교.x: My younger sibling goes to a university in Seoul.
대학교.t: Pronounced [대학꾜]. In speech 대학 alone is also common: 대학에 가요.

싫어하다.x: My younger sibling doesn't like vegetables.
싫어하다.e: 싫다 (unpleasant) + -어하다. 싫어요! = No, I don't want to!
싫어하다.t: Pronounced [시러하다]: ㅎ in ㅀ is silent before a vowel.

짧다.x: These pants are too short for me.
짧다.e: Opposite of 길다; 짧은 머리 = short hair.
짧다.t: Pronounced [짤따]; 짧아요 [짤바요]. For a short person, say 키가 작다, not 짧다.

귀엽다.x: My friend's puppy is really cute.
귀엽다.e: 귀여워요! Acting cute is called 애교 (aegyo), big in K-pop.

지각하다.m: to be late (for school or work)
지각하다.x: I overslept and was late for work.
지각하다.t: 지각하다 is for school or work; for meeting friends just say 늦다.

이상.ex: 이 영화는 열다섯 살 이상만 볼 수 있어요.
이상.x: Only people aged fifteen and over can see this movie.
이상.t: 이상 includes the number itself: 20세 이상 means 20 and older. A different 이상 means 'strange'.

이상.ex: 이상과 현실 사이에는 늘 차이가 있어요.
이상.x: There is always a gap between ideals and reality.
이상.e: Literally 'reasoned thought' — the way things should be.
이상.t: Don't confuse with homonyms 이상 'more than' and 이상 'strange, abnormal'.

수입.x: My store's income has gone down lately, so I'm worried.
수입.e: Literally 'taking in'. A homonym 수입 (different hanja) means 'import'.

변경.x: Sorry, there's been a sudden change in the schedule.

지적하다.x: My teacher pointed out the problems in my presentation.
지적하다.e: Literally 'point at and pick out' a flaw.
지적하다.t: Don't confuse it with the different word 지적 meaning 'intellectual,' as in 지적인 사람.

회복되다.x: After a good rest, my health recovered a lot.
회복되다.t: Pronounced [회복뙤다] — ㄷ after ㄱ becomes tense.

수명.ex: 한국 사람들의 평균 수명이 점점 길어지고 있습니다.
수명.x: The average life expectancy of Koreans is getting longer and longer.

꿀꺽.x: I swallowed the pill with water in one gulp.
꿀꺽.e: Sound and manner word (의성어·의태어) for swallowing at once. Bright-vowel 꼴깍 is a smaller, lighter swallow.
꿀꺽.t: 침을 꿀꺽 삼키다 = 'to gulp nervously' or at tempting food. 꿀꺽하다 is also slang for pocketing money dishonestly.

멋대로.forms: 멋대로 + verb (멋대로 하다); 제멋대로 = as one pleases
멋대로.m: as one pleases, at will, selfishly
멋대로.ex: 남의 물건을 멋대로 쓰면 안 돼요.
멋대로.x: You shouldn't use other people's things as you please.
멋대로.e: 멋 'one's own taste' + 대로 'as, according to'.
멋대로.t: Negative tone; 마음대로 is the neutral 'freely, as you like'.

허용하다.x: This restaurant allows you to bring pets.
허용하다.t: 허용하다 is about rules and systems; 허락하다 is a person giving permission.

받치다.m: to support, prop up; to hold (an umbrella) over; to wear underneath
받치다.ex: 무거운 상자를 두 손으로 받쳐서 옮겼어요.
받치다.x: I carried the heavy box, supporting it with both hands.
받치다.t: Sounds just like 바치다 'to offer, dedicate'; spelling tells them apart.

천생연분.m: a match made in heaven, soulmates
천생연분.ex: 두 사람은 정말 천생연분인 것 같아요.
천생연분.x: Those two really seem like a match made in heaven.

결핍.ex: 비타민 결핍은 여러 가지 질병을 일으킬 수 있습니다.
결핍.x: Vitamin deficiency can cause various diseases.
결핍.e: Both syllables mean 'lacking,' doubling the idea.
결핍.t: 부족 is the everyday 'lack'; 결핍 sounds more serious, as in medical or psychological contexts.

파급.ex: 그 정책은 사회 전체에 큰 파급을 미쳤어요.
파급.x: That policy had ripple effects across the whole society.
파급.e: Literally 'waves reaching': like ripples spreading across water.

세력.x: A new political force has emerged.

실업률.x: The youth unemployment rate has gone up compared to last year.

편향.ex: 사람은 누구나 자신도 모르는 편향을 가지고 있어요.
편향.x: Everyone has biases they aren't even aware of.

규명하다.m: to investigate and clarify, to get to the bottom of
규명하다.ex: 경찰은 사고 원인을 규명하기 위해 조사를 시작했습니다.
규명하다.x: The police began an investigation to find out the cause of the accident.

피력하다.m: to express, to state (one's opinion) openly
피력하다.ex: 그는 회의에서 자신의 의견을 솔직하게 피력했어요.
피력하다.x: He openly expressed his opinion at the meeting.
피력하다.e: Literally 'opening up and pouring out' one's thoughts.

허황되다.ex: 허황된 꿈만 꾸지 말고 계획을 세우세요.
허황되다.x: Don't just chase unrealistic dreams; make a plan.
허황되다.t: Mostly used as a modifier: 허황된 꿈, 허황된 욕심.

동고동락.m: sharing joys and sorrows, going through thick and thin together
동고동락.x: We're colleagues who've been through thick and thin together for ten years.
동고동락.t: Pronounced [동고동낙]; usually as the verb 동고동락하다.

배보다 배꼽이 더 크다.forms: 배보다 배꼽이 더 커요 · 배보다 배꼽이 더 컸어요
배보다 배꼽이 더 크다.m: the extras cost more than the main thing; the tail wagging the dog
배보다 배꼽이 더 크다.ex: 프린터보다 잉크가 더 비싸서 배보다 배꼽이 더 커요.
배보다 배꼽이 더 크다.x: The ink costs more than the printer; the extras cost more than the main item.
배보다 배꼽이 더 크다.e: Literally 'the belly button is bigger than the belly.'
rel: to put the cart before the horse
nb: 개구리 올챙이 적 생각 못 한다

서당.x: Long ago, children learned the Thousand Character Classic at village schools.
서당.t: The proverb 서당 개 삼 년 means even a dog picks up skills after three years nearby.

구직난.x: Young people's difficulty finding jobs gets worse every year.
구직난.e: Literally 'job-seeking hardship'. -난 = shortage, crisis: 구직난, 전세난.
구직난.t: Pronounced [구징난] — nasalization; compare 구인난, where employers struggle to find workers.

혼란스럽다.x: There's so much information that my head feels confused.
혼란스럽다.e: Literally 'mixed up and in disorder'. -스럽다 turns a noun into 'feeling like X'.
혼란스럽다.t: Pronounced [홀란스럽따] — ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

임상 시험.ex: 새로운 약은 임상 시험을 거쳐야 판매할 수 있습니다.
임상 시험.x: A new drug can only be sold after going through clinical trials.
임상 시험.e: Literally 'testing at the bedside' — trials on real patients.

전자 상거래.ex: 요즘은 전자 상거래로 물건을 사는 사람이 많아요.
전자 상거래.x: These days, many people buy things through e-commerce.
전자 상거래.e: Literally 'electronic trade'; 거래 'deal' is literally 'going and coming.'
전자 상거래.t: In business news it's also called 이커머스, from English 'e-commerce.'

밀약.ex: 두 나라 사이에 밀약이 있었다는 사실이 드러났습니다.
밀약.x: It came to light that there had been a secret pact between the two countries.
밀약.t: Pronounced [미략]; 밀약을 맺다 = to make a secret pact.

안전보장이사회.x: The Security Council condemned North Korea's missile launch.
안전보장이사회.t: News nearly always uses the short form 안보리.

강박증.ex: 그는 문을 여러 번 확인하는 강박증이 있어요.
강박증.x: He has an obsessive habit of checking the door many times.

고지혈증.ex: 기름진 음식을 많이 먹으면 고지혈증에 걸리기 쉬워요.
고지혈증.x: Eating a lot of fatty food makes you prone to high cholesterol.

경공업.ex: 1960년대 한국 경제는 섬유 같은 경공업이 중심이었습니다.
경공업.x: In the 1960s, Korea's economy centered on light industries like textiles.
경공업.e: Literally 'light industry'; the opposite is 중공업.

가락.ex: 할아버지는 흥겨운 가락에 맞춰 어깨춤을 추셨어요.
가락.x: Grandpa danced with his shoulders to the cheerful tune.
가락.e: Homonym: 가락 also means a long thin piece, as in 손가락 and 젓가락.
가락.t: Also a counter for thin strands: 국수 한 가락 means one strand of noodles.

음색.ex: 그 가수는 맑고 독특한 음색으로 사랑받고 있어요.
음색.x: That singer is loved for her clear, distinctive voice.
음색.e: Literally 'sound color', just like English 'tone color'.

득의양양.m: elation and triumph, being puffed up with pride
득의양양.ex: 시험에 합격한 동생이 득의양양한 표정을 지었어요.
득의양양.x: My younger sibling, having passed the exam, looked triumphant.
득의양양.e: Literally 'having gotten one's wish, spirits soaring high'.

조령모개.m: orders that change constantly, inconsistent policy
조령모개.ex: 조령모개식 정책 때문에 시민들의 불만이 커지고 있습니다.
조령모개.x: Citizens are growing frustrated with policies that change constantly.
조령모개.e: Literally 'an order in the morning, changed by evening'.
조령모개.t: Usually criticism of government: 조령모개식 정책 'flip-flopping policy'.

조성하다.m: to create, to build (an atmosphere, environment, fund); to develop (a park, site)
조성하다.x: The city created a park along the riverbank.
조성하다.t: Common objects: 분위기, 환경, 공원, 기금 — creating something that wasn't there.

투박하다.m: rough, crude, coarse; blunt, unpolished (speech or manner)
투박하다.ex: 할아버지는 말투가 투박하지만 정이 정말 많으세요.
투박하다.x: My grandfather talks bluntly, but he's really warm-hearted.
투박하다.e: Used for objects and manners that look clumsy but are often sturdy and honest.

소외계층.ex: 이 단체는 소외계층 아이들에게 무료 교육을 제공합니다.
소외계층.x: This organization provides free education to underprivileged children.
소외계층.e: Literally 'kept-outside stratum': people left out of society's benefits.

헛되다.ex: 그동안 열심히 한 노력이 헛되지 않았어요.
헛되다.x: All the hard work I put in was not in vain.
헛되다.e: 헛- 'empty, in vain' (as in 헛소리) + 되다.
헛되다.t: Pronounced [헏뙤다]; common in 헛된 꿈 'a vain dream'.
